paragraphs: Abba Shaul ben Botnit. In the Mishnah at the end of Ein Tzadin: Abba Shaul ben Botnit used to fill his measures on the eve of a festival and give them to customers on the festival. Abba Shaul says: they do so even during the intermediate days, because of the settling of the measures; see the Gemara there. He collected three hundred jars of wine from the settling of the measures and brought them to Jerusalem's treasurers. They would not accept them, but told him to use them for public needs. Rashi explains that he was a great sage and filled his measures at night to avoid interrupting study. Yuhasin, in its account of R' Tzadok, says that R' Abba, R' Elazar bar Tzadok and Abba Shaul ben Botnit were shopkeepers in Jerusalem all their lives and filled their measures on the eve of a festival. Heilprin says he does not know who R' Abba was. Heilprin cites Tosefta Beitzah chapter 3. Its parallel at 3:6 names the last two. The checked Yuhasin labels its source Tosefta Sukkah chapter 3. Heilprin questions whether R' Elazar bar Tzadok was Abba Shaul ben Botnit’s contemporary. Mishnah Shabbat 24:5 places the incident in which they stopped the window with an earthenware vessel in the days of R' Tzadok’s father and Abba Shaul ben Botnit. Makom She-Nahagu (Pesahim 57a) quotes Abba Shaul about sycamore beams in Jericho. Powerful men took them, so their owners consecrated them. Abba Shaul ben Botnit then speaks in Abba Yosi ben Hanan’s name. The checked Bavli reads Abba Yosef ben Hanin. Tosefta, Menahot chapter 13: ‘Concerning them Abba Shaul ben Botnit said; Abba Yosi ben Yohanan, a man of Jerusalem, says,’ etc. Two explanations are possible: either Abba Shaul ben Botnit, or Abba Shaul reporting what Abba Shaul ben Botnit, who preceded him, said. Rambam likewise listed them as two. His son Botnit (see there) was in Rabbi's time.
